notes:
Summary: Marlow Edge evaluated Redwood for low-latency edge inference across robotics fleets. Strong initial interest from product & platform teams. Primary drivers: strict data residency, deterministic latency for edge controllers, cost control at scale. Decision: closed-lost — internal infra team will self-host using vLLM/TGI and TensorRT-LLM optimizations. Key quotes: "We need kernel-level control and hardware-direct deployment — hosted model won't fly for our safety team." 

Security: Security and compliance ran a deep checklist; SSO + audit logging OK but residency and 3rd-party managed KMS flagged. They asked for on-prem air-gapped option; our private offering answered some items but internal procurement pushed for owning everything.

Commercial: initial pricing looked competitive, but after procurement's TCO model (3yr) the self-host option wins on per-token cost with batching/quantization. Also employee_count and fleet scale tipped economics.

Internal dynamics: after a VP-level org change the internal champion (Lead ML Infra) moved to a different role, and the new team prefers in-house ops. There is curiosity about Redwood Optimize recommendations, but no timeline.

Next actions captured: 1) Mark closed-lost; 2) Add to watchlist for infra pain signals (latency spikes, model ops cost); 3) Offer a short post-mortem doc & migration checklist for when they consider hybrid.

Stated blockers on the final call: budget freeze, internal champion left, and strategic mandate to self-host for control.
